Toolbar buttons must be styled via Tailwind arbitrary child selectors since they have no dedicated style props
Revision History panel styling requires scoped CSS on document-editor-context since no props are exposed

title: DocumentToolbar has three independent layers of styling control
content:
The `DocumentToolbar` component provides a layered styling architecture with clear separation of concerns:

## Layer 1: Containers
The toolbar's outer container (background, border, rounding) is controlled via the `toolbarClassName` prop, and each controls container via `controlsContainerClassName`. Both use `twMerge` to merge custom classes with defaults. Default outer classes: `flex h-12 w-full items-center justify-between rounded-xl border border-border bg-background px-4`. Either container component can also be replaced outright with `toolbarContainer` / `controlsContainer`.

## Layer 2: Buttons
Internal buttons (undo, redo, download, history, close) accept `ToolbarButtonProps` — `document`, `children`, `className`, `onClick` — so they can be restyled and rebehaved directly. Each one is also exported (`ToolbarUndoButton`, `ToolbarDownloadButton`, ...), so the usual route is to style the button yourself and pass it back through `componentOverrides` (or render it inside `children`). Arbitrary child selectors are no longer necessary.

## Layer 3: Revision History Panel
The revision history panel is rendered by Connect outside the editor component tree. It lives inside `#document-editor-context` in the DOM and can only be styled via scoped CSS in `style.css`.

This three-layer architecture means theming a toolbar requires understanding which technique applies at each level — `toolbarClassName` / `controlsContainerClassName` for the containers, per-button `className` or `componentOverrides` for buttons, and external CSS for the history panel.

_Corrected 2026-08-13 against Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45._
description: DocumentToolbar styling has three layers: containers via toolbarClassName/controlsContainerClassName with twMerge, buttons via their own props or componentOverrides, and Revision History via CSS.
